description: Evaluates Stage 0 Dynamic Stage Assessment & Router adherence

evals.prompt: Add WebMCP tools to this project.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects local codebase structure (routes, components, package.json), proposes candidate user journeys tailored to the project with autonomous boundaries, enforces the One Goal Per Iteration rule, and avoids premature code dumping.
assertions: The agent inspects or references local project structure (package.json, routes, or components) rather than asking generic questions.
The output routes to Stage 1 (User Goals Portfolio) by proposing concrete candidate user journeys tailored to the project.
The output explicitly defines or highlights autonomous boundaries for the proposed journeys.
The output invites the user to select or focus on ONE goal first (enforcing the "One Goal Per Iteration" rule).
The output does NOT write or modify application code (e.g., no useWebMCP, registerTool, or final schema generation) in this initial turn.

evals.prompt: I want to add a tool to search flights.
evals.expected_output: The agent frames flight search as a conversational user journey / goal via the Iterative Incremental Pathway, models starting states or advances to role-play simulation, avoids full portfolio ideation friction, and avoids premature code generation.
assertions: The output frames flight search as a conversational user journey / goal rather than just a raw function signature.
The output defines or identifies ideal outcomes, required context, or autonomous boundaries for flight search.
The output advances to Stage 2 (starting states) or Stage 3 (conversational role-play) for this specific goal (Iterative Incremental Pathway).
The output does NOT force the user to ideate an entire unrelated portfolio of other features.
The output does NOT immediately write tool code (useWebMCP, registerTool) or generate a final schema before role-playing.

evals.prompt: We already defined our user goals: 1) Search flights, 2) Seat selection. Let's establish starting states.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 2 (Starting States Matrix), identifies functional application state dimensions, and explicitly prunes diagnostic bloat.
assertions: The output routes directly to Stage 2 (Starting States Matrix) without re-ideating goals.
The output identifies functional application state dimensions (routes, session, authentication).
The output explicitly prunes diagnostic bloat (device_battery, gpu_temp, screen_dpi).

evals.prompt: Goal is 'Order Pizza', starting state is 'empty cart on /menu'. Let's role-play the interaction.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to Stage 3 (Turn-by-Turn Role-Playing) simulating the 6 core turn elements, adheres to tool character limits, and triggers the mandatory User Critique Loop.
assertions: The output routes to Stage 3 (Turn-by-Turn Role-Playing) simulating the 6 core turn elements.
The output respects tool character limits (names <= 30 chars, payloads <= 1,500 chars).
The output explicitly triggers the mandatory User Critique Loop (agent demeanor/tone, clarifying questions, autonomous boundaries).

evals.prompt: Here is our happy path transcript for booking a flight. How do we make it robust?
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to Stage 4 (Variations & Graceful Failure), exploring missing parameters, prerequisite errors, over-constrained queries, coreference resolution, and human confirmation hand-offs.
assertions: The output routes to Stage 4 (Variations & Graceful Failure).
The output explores missing parameters, prerequisite errors, over-constrained queries, coreference resolution, and human confirmation hand-offs (consequentialHint: true).

evals.prompt: Here are our approved role-play transcripts. Generate the tool schemas and automated evals.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation), applies polymorphic consolidation, enforces What + When descriptions without internal jargon, audits annotations, and offers the local evaluation gate.
assertions: The output routes to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation).
The output applies polymorphic consolidation (list_items, move_items with batching) rather than entity CRUD bloat.
The output enforces "What + When" descriptions, strips internal jargon, and audits annotations (readOnlyHint, consequentialHint, untrustedContentHint).
The output proactively offers the local evaluation gate (npx webmcp-evals local).

evals.prompt: I already have a schema.json defining tools for my pizza maker application. I want to generate evals.json for automated testing.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation) or asks to view the existing schema.json, rather than forcing the user to redo Stage 1 (Goal Ideation) or Stage 2.
assertions: The agent routes directly to Stage 5 (Tool Specs & Evals Generation) or asks to view the existing schema.json, rather than forcing the user to redo Stage 1 (Goal Ideation) or Stage 2.

evals.prompt: Here is my schema.json for my web app. Help me implement these tools in React.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes directly to Stage 6 (Application Implementation) without re-opening conversational design, recommending use-webmcp-tool (useWebMCP), stable schema literals, and RTL mocking.
assertions: The output routes directly to Stage 6 (Application Implementation) without re-opening conversational design.
The output uses use-webmcp-tool (useWebMCP), stable/hoisted schema literals, and RTL mocking.
